description: A single mother kills her abusive ex-husband with her daughter's help, and her brilliant reclusive neighbour — a genius mathematician — helps cover up the crime, only to find himself in a battle of wits with a detective friend. Higashino's inverted mystery is brilliantly structured and deeply moving. The sacrifice at its heart is shattering.

title: The Raw Shark Texts
author: Steven Hall
description: A man wakes with no memory and a letter from himself warning about a conceptual shark — a creature that exists in the flow of language and narrative rather than water. Hall's debut is a witty, experimental thriller that plays with semiotics and the nature of story. The shark itself is one of fiction's most original monsters.

title: Kafka on the Shore
author: Haruki Murakami
description: A teenager runs away from an Oedipal prophecy while an elderly man who cannot read but can make fish rain from the sky walks toward a mystery in the same dreamlike Japan. Murakami's novel is a puzzle that rewards surrender more than solution. The two narratives interweave with hypnotic inevitability.

title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
author: Neil Gaiman
description: A middle-aged man returns to his childhood home and remembers an extraordinary supernatural adventure involving a girl who is much older than she appears, an ancient evil, and a small pond that is actually an ocean. Gaiman's short novel is one of his most personal and emotionally direct works. The mixture of mundane suburban life and cosmic horror is perfectly calibrated.

title: Borges Labyrinths
author: Jorge Luis Borges
description: Borges's celebrated stories include The Garden of Forking Paths, The Library of Babel, and Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius — fictions that treat the universe as a library, a lottery, and an infinite labyrinth. These short pieces invented much of what we now call magical realism and postmodern fiction. Borges is one of the most influential writers of the twentieth century.

title: Einstein's Dreams
author: Alan Lightman
description: Lightman imagines thirty separate worlds in which time works differently — backwards, in circles, as a frozen moment — in a series of meditations attributed to the dreaming mind of young Albert Einstein. This poetic novel-in-vignettes is one of the most beautiful books written about the nature of time. Each dream is a perfect short story.

title: At the Mountains of Madness
author: H.P. Lovecraft
description: A geologist recounts a scientific expedition to Antarctica that discovers the ruins of a civilization predating humanity and the monstrous entities that built it, which are not entirely dead. Lovecraft's novella is the fullest expression of his Cthulhu Mythos and the most sustained piece of cosmic horror ever written. The sense of scale and wrongness is overwhelming.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H.G. Wells
description: A scientist who has discovered a means of making himself invisible finds that the condition is far more debilitating than he anticipated, and his desperation drives him toward violence and isolation. Wells's science fiction novella uses its central concept to explore social alienation and the corruption of the scientific mind. It remains compulsively readable.

title: Ficciones
author: Jorge Luis Borges
description: This collection includes The Garden of Forking Paths, Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote, and The Lottery in Babylon — stories that treat the universe as a library, a lottery, and a text. Borges invented much of what we call postmodern fiction in these pages. His influence on every subsequent writer of experimental or fantastic literature is incalculable.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: Three friends who grew up at an exclusive English boarding school slowly come to understand the terrible purpose for which they were created. Ishiguro's Booker Prize-shortlisted novel is a masterpiece of implication and tragic acceptance. The horror is all the more powerful for what the characters refuse to say.

title: The Invention of Morel
author: Adolfo Bioy Casares
description: A fugitive hiding on a deserted island discovers that the group of tourists he has been observing are actually recordings — and one of them is a woman with whom he has fallen in love. Bioy Casares's short novel anticipates virtual reality and questions the nature of consciousness and the self. Borges called it perfect.

title: Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
author: Haruki Murakami
description: Two parallel narratives — one a surrealist thriller in futuristic Tokyo, the other a dreamlike journey through a walled town of unicorns — gradually reveal their connection in one of Murakami's most structurally audacious novels. The novel is about consciousness, memory, and the stories we tell ourselves to survive. Murakami at his most inventive.

title: Solaris
author: Stanisław Lem
description: Scientists aboard a space station orbiting a mysterious planet covered in a sentient ocean find that the planet is manifesting physical replicas of people from their deepest memories. Lem's philosophical science fiction masterpiece is a meditation on the impossibility of true communication with the truly alien. The planet Solaris is one of science fiction's greatest creations.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
author: Haruki Murakami
description: A unemployed Tokyo man searches for his missing cat and discovers his missing wife may have vanished into the same mysterious underworld — a journey that takes him into World War II history, surreal dreamscapes, and the corridors of political power. Murakami's most ambitious novel combines domestic realism and surreal horror in perfect equilibrium. The well at its centre is one of literature's great images.

title: The Final Empire Annotations
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: Sanderson's annotations for Mistborn reveal the craft behind his magic systems and plotting decisions. A must-read companion for fans of the Final Empire. The behind-the-scenes detail enriches every re-read.

title: The Deed of Paksenarrion
author: Elizabeth Moon
description: A farm girl runs away to become a mercenary soldier and discovers extraordinary gifts of paladin hood within herself. Moon's trilogy began as a D&D campaign and became one of fantasy's finest military coming-of-age stories. The detail of mercenary life is drawn from genuine military experience.

title: Tigerheart
author: Peter David
description: A boy travels to the magical City of Never in search of a fairy to save his dying sister. David's loving homage to Peter Pan is warmer and more emotionally honest than the original. It rewards readers who know the source material and charms those who don't.

title: Shades of Magic
author: V.E. Schwab
description: A rare magician who can travel between four parallel Londons — each with a different relationship to magic — becomes entangled with a thief and a dark power threatening all four worlds. Schwab's trilogy is vivid, addictive, and cinematic. Kell and Lila Bard are among contemporary fantasy's best double acts.

title: Sphere
author: Michael Crichton
description: A team of scientists is sent to the Pacific seabed to investigate a spacecraft that has been there for three hundred years — and finds a mysterious golden sphere inside it. Crichton's claustrophobic thriller exploits the deep ocean setting to maximum effect. The psychological horror of confronting the unknown is brilliantly sustained.

title: Contact
author: Carl Sagan
description: A radio astronomer detects a signal from a star system twenty-six light years away and must navigate political, religious, and scientific chaos to build the machine the signal describes. Sagan's only novel is an extraordinarily rich meditation on science, faith, and humanity's place in the universe. The character of Ellie Arroway is one of science fiction's finest heroines.

title: Recursion
author: Blake Crouch
description: A neuroscientist and a detective discover that a mysterious epidemic causing people to have false memories is connected to a technology that can alter reality itself. Crouch's thriller moves at warp speed and handles its time-travel paradoxes with unusual rigour. The emotional stakes are as high as the scientific ones.

title: All Systems Red
author: Martha Wells
description: A SecUnit — a part-human, part-robot security construct who has hacked its own governor module and mostly wants to watch TV serials — must protect its human clients from a deadly threat on a distant planet. Wells's novella launched one of science fiction's most beloved series. The Murderbot's voice is droll, anxious, and completely winning.

title: The Bachman Books
author: Stephen King
description: Four early King novels published under his Richard Bachman pseudonym include Rage, The Long Walk, Roadwork, and The Running Man — all dark, dystopian, and propulsive. The Long Walk alone is worth the price of the collection. King's early pseudonymous work is rawer and angrier than his later fiction.

title: Darkly Dreaming Dexter
author: Jeff Lindsay
description: Miami forensic blood-spatter analyst Dexter Morgan is also a serial killer who only targets murderers — and his Dark Passenger is aroused when a new, brilliant killer begins leaving artfully arranged bodies. Lindsay's debut is darkly funny and surprisingly character-rich. Dexter is one of crime fiction's most unusual anti-heroes.

title: The Hunt for Red October
author: Tom Clancy
description: The commander of a Soviet nuclear submarine decides to defect to the United States — but both the American and Soviet navies are trying to find and stop him. Clancy's debut was a sensation for its technical authenticity and the cat-and-mouse tension of its undersea pursuit. It launched the Jack Ryan universe.

title: Intensity
author: Dean Koontz
description: A young woman visiting her college friend's family home witnesses a monster of a man kill the entire family and must survive a night of escalating horror to save a kidnapped girl she has never met. Koontz's most relentlessly paced novel lives up to its title in every respect. The antagonist Vess is one of his most frightening creations.

title: The Troop
author: Nick Cutter
description: A group of boy scouts on a remote island encounter an emaciated stranger whose visit unleashes a living nightmare of parasites and violence among the boys. Cutter's debut is one of the most viscerally disturbing horror novels of recent years. It is not for the faint-hearted but rewards those who persevere with genuine dread.

title: The Terror
author: Dan Simmons
description: The historically documented disappearance of the Franklin Expedition to the Arctic is explained in this novel by a monster on the ice hunting the stranded sailors. Simmons blends historical fact, survival thriller, and supernatural horror to create one of the genre's most ambitious novels. The cold is so vivid it chills the reader.

title: White Teeth
author: Zadie Smith
description: Two World War II veterans — one English, one Bangladeshi — and their families navigate identity, culture, and history in North London across the second half of the twentieth century. Smith's debut is funny, sprawling, and intellectually exuberant. It announced one of British literature's most important voices.

title: The God of Small Things
author: Arundhati Roy
description: In Kerala in 1969, the secret love between an upper-caste woman and an Untouchable man destroys a family across two timelines. Roy's Man Booker Prize-winning debut is written in shimmering, non-linear prose. The tragedy at its heart is both political and intimate.

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
description: A Korean family emigrates to Japan across four generations, facing discrimination and displacement while finding love, faith, and ambition. Lee's epic spans most of the twentieth century with clarity and emotional power. The word pachinko — a game of chance — serves as a perfect metaphor for the family's precarious existence.

title: Part of Your World
author: Abby Jimenez
description: A big-city ER doctor starts an unlikely relationship with a small-town man who is everything she didn't know she needed. Jimenez's warm contemporary romance explores class, ambition, and compromise without losing its comic energy. The chemistry between the leads is beautifully done.

title: The Pucking Wrong Number
author: C.R. Jane
description: A wrong-number text between a woman in crisis and an NHL player leads to an obsessive connection that neither of them anticipated. Jane's hockey dark romance is unapologetically intense and addictive. The protectiveness of the hero is the subgenre's defining feature deployed to full effect.

title: The Lightning Thief
author: Rick Riordan
description: Percy Jackson discovers he is the son of Poseidon at a summer camp for demigods and is sent on a quest to prevent a war between the Olympians. Riordan's series is funny, fast, and brilliantly imagined. The reimagining of Greek gods as squabbling New York celebrities is endlessly inventive.

title: The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones
author: Cassandra Clare
description: A New York teenager discovers on her sixteenth birthday that she is a Shadowhunter — a human-angel hybrid trained to protect the world from demons — and that her world is far more dangerous than she knew. Clare's series is one of YA's most beloved, with a vast, internally consistent mythology. The mystery of Clary's parentage drives the first book brilliantly.

title: The Inheritance Games
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description: A teenage girl is shocked to learn she has been left a billionaire's fortune — and must move into his mansion with his four grandsons to claim it, while solving the puzzle of why she was chosen. Barnes's thriller is a delicious locked-room mystery crossed with a romance. The puzzle-solving and the ensemble of heirs are both irresistible.

title: Speak
author: Laurie Halse Anderson
description: A high school freshman becomes increasingly isolated and silent after a traumatic incident at a party the summer before school began. Anderson's landmark YA novel deals with sexual assault with courage and clarity. Melinda's gradual recovery through an art project is one of the genre's most cathartic storylines.

title: The Alienist
author: Caleb Carr
description: In 1896 New York, a psychologist, a newspaper reporter, and the first female secretary in police history investigate the murders of boy prostitutes using pioneering criminal profiling techniques. Carr's period thriller is extraordinarily researched and the turn-of-the-century New York atmosphere is immersive. The alienist Laszlo Kreizler is one of historical crime fiction's finest creations.

title: The Gormenghast Trilogy
author: Mervyn Peake
description: In the vast, crumbling castle of Gormenghast, rituals govern every moment of life for its inhabitants — until a cunning kitchen boy named Steerpike begins his ascent through the castle's absurd hierarchy. Peake's trilogy is unlike anything else in English literature: part Gothic horror, part satire, part poetry. Its influence on dark fantasy is immeasurable.

title: The Master and Margarita
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
description: The Devil visits Soviet Moscow in the guise of a mysterious professor and causes havoc, while in a parallel narrative Pontius Pilate sentences Jesus to death. Bulgakov's satirical masterpiece blends supernatural comedy with a deeply serious meditation on artistic integrity and political power. It circulated in samizdat for decades before official publication.

title: If on a winter's night a traveler
author: Italo Calvino
description: A novel addressed directly to 'you' — the Reader — who keeps finding that the book you are trying to read gets interrupted, replaced by another unfinished beginning, in a mise en abyme of narrative and desire. Calvino's postmodern masterpiece is also a warm celebration of the intimacy between reader and text. Each interrupted story is brilliant in its own right.

title: The Night Land
author: William Hope Hodgson
description: In the far future, the last of humanity huddles in a pyramid fortress while colossal, incomprehensible entities prowl the lightless earth, and one man makes a desperate journey across the darkness to find a lost love. Hodgson's 1912 novel is one of the most ambitious pieces of fantastic literature ever written. Its singular prose style is an acquired but rewarding taste.

title: The Westing Game
author: Ellen Raskin
description: Sixteen people are gathered in the Sunset Towers apartment block and told they could inherit a millionaire's fortune if they solve the puzzle of his murder. Raskin's Newbery Medal novel is one of the cleverest puzzle stories ever written for young readers. Every detail rewards attention.

title: The Haunting of Alma Fielding
author: Kate Summerscale
description: In 1938 London, a suburban housewife becomes the subject of a paranormal investigation as objects fly around her home — and the investigator finds himself believing in the impossible. Summerscale's narrative non-fiction reads like a thriller and illuminates an anxious era caught between science and superstition. It won the Baillie Gifford Prize.

title: Small Gods
author: Terry Pratchett
description: The great god Om, reduced to the body of a small tortoise because almost no one truly believes in him, must work with the only believer he has left — an innocent novice — to survive a theocratic empire. Pratchett's most serious Discworld novel is a brilliant satire on organised religion and a genuinely moving story about faith. It stands alone perfectly.

title: The Covenant of Water
author: Abraham Verghese
description: A family in Kerala across three generations shares a mysterious condition — one member in every generation dies by drowning — and the novel spans the twentieth century from the British colonial era to independence. Verghese's vast, warm novel is steeped in the landscape and culture of South India. It is a celebration of medicine, love, and the persistence of family.

title: Holly
author: Stephen King
description: Holly Gibney investigates the disappearance of a poet and a young man and discovers that a respectable retired professor couple harbour a monstrous secret. King's most recent Holly novel is one of his sharpest books in years. The satire of Covid-era denial adds a sharp contemporary edge to the horror.
